---
title: "Classifying codes with an LLM ensemble"
format: html
---

Drafts the mapping of every USRDS primary-cause code to the six categories of the paper's Table 1, using three large language models, for review by the deciders ([#D4]). It is run once, by hand, because it calls paid APIs; the reviewed file in `references/` is what the analysis reads.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/classify_esrd_causes.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/classify_esrd_causes.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/classify_esrd_causes.R")
```

## ellmer version

The script needs ellmer 0.4.2 or later. From that version, ellmer uses Anthropic's own structured output for current Claude models; earlier versions force a tool call, which these models reject.

```{r}
#| label: check-ellmer-version
#| eval: false
```

## The code list

The original mapping spreadsheet is lost. Its replacement starts from a public list: every code of USRDS format `$PD96DET` with its description, from Appendix C of the Researcher's Guide, which `usRds` already holds. No patient data are involved, and the list is not filtered by what appears in the data.

```{r}
#| label: load-cause-codes
#| eval: false
```

## The prompt

All three models receive the same prompt, word for word. It is kept as a text file, [`prompts/esrd-cause-classification.md`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/prompts/esrd-cause-classification.md), so that it can be read and edited on its own and shown here exactly as sent:

```{verbatim}
#| file: ../prompts/esrd-cause-classification.md
#| lang: markdown
```

For each batch of 100 codes, `{{code_list}}` becomes one line per code: the code, a colon and the USRDS description from the Researcher's Guide (for example, `4464Z: WEGENERS GRANULOMATOSIS`). Nothing else about a code is sent. The script stops if the prompt does not define each of the six categories, under exactly the names in `setup.R`, because the structured output can only return those names.

The prompt makes three rules:

-   **One category per code**, from the six in the paper's Table 1, each defined in words.
-   **"Other" is the catch-all**, for every cause outside the first five and for codes that mean missing, unknown or unreconcilable, as in the original analysis.
-   **No inference beyond the description.** The model classifies from the code and its description only, which keeps it from inventing context.

## The six categories

::: callout-warning
## Draft definitions
The definitions in the prompt are placeholders, written to show how the classification is specified. The deciders settle the real ones (open decision [#D4]).
:::

The original analysis took the six categories from a spreadsheet with one sheet per category ("Diabetes", "Hypertensive and Cardiac", "Glomerulonephritis", "HereditaryPCKD", "Transplant", "Other"), which no longer exists. Only the categories' names survive, in the sheet names and in the paper's Table 1, which labels the transplant category "solid organ and bone marrow" [@hemmige2024density].

The draft definitions follow the USRDS primary disease groups, the groups of the CMS-2728 list of primary causes [@cms2728_causes; @usrds2018adr]:

| Paper category | Draft definition, in USRDS groups |
|---|---|
| Diabetes | Diabetes |
| Hypertension and cardiac disease | Hypertension and large vessel disease (including renovascular disease and atheroembolism), plus kidney failure attributed to heart disease, as the sheet name "Hypertensive and Cardiac" suggests |
| Glomerulonephritis | Glomerulonephritis (primary glomerular disease) |
| Hereditary or polycystic kidney disease | The cystic and hereditary part of "Cystic/hereditary/congenital", as the sheet name "HereditaryPCKD" suggests; congenital anomalies go to Other |
| Transplant failure or complications | Transplant complications of any solid organ or bone marrow, as Table 1 says (USRDS counted these among miscellaneous conditions until the 2015 form gave them their own group) |
| Other | Secondary glomerulonephritis and vasculitis, interstitial nephritis and pyelonephritis, congenital anomalies, neoplasms, miscellaneous conditions, and unknown or missing causes |

**HIV.** USRDS has always placed HIV-associated (AIDS) nephropathy among the miscellaneous conditions, not with glomerulonephritis: in its older reference tables, and as code B20 in the "Miscellaneous conditions" group of the 2015 CMS-2728 list [@cms2728_causes]. The draft therefore puts HIV in Other. The three models did the same on the first run.

**What the paper's Table 1 can and cannot show.** In the published cohort, the six categories were diabetes 48.0%, hypertension and cardiac disease 29.5%, glomerulonephritis 5.7%, hereditary or polycystic kidney disease 1.9%, transplant 0.5% and other 14.3% (computed from the Table 1 counts). Among all incident patients in 2016, USRDS reported glomerulonephritis at 7.3% and cystic kidney disease at 2.8% [@usrds2018adr]. The paper's lower shares fit glomerulonephritis without its secondary forms, and polycystic and hereditary disease without congenital anomalies. But the cohort is in-center hemodialysis only, and patients with glomerulonephritis or polycystic kidney disease more often start on peritoneal dialysis or receive a transplant, so the comparison cannot settle either boundary. Small groups such as HIV are invisible in these percentages.

## Prompt and schema in code

The structured output schema restricts each answer to the six category names, and the check below confirms it. Each saved answer file carries a short fingerprint of the prompt text, so an edited prompt is sent to every provider again.

```{r}
#| label: define-classification-prompt
#| eval: false
```

## One function per provider

The same three providers as the USRDS-PDF-analysis-project ensemble, each with its current general-purpose model, set in `setup.R` [@ellmer_pkg]. Each has its own function, so each provider can be run, checked and saved on its own.

```{r}
#| label: define-providers
#| eval: false
```

## Running and saving each provider

Each provider runs and is checked on its own: every code answered exactly once, no invented codes, only the six categories. Its answers are then saved under the provider and model name, so a rerun after a failure asks only the providers that have not finished.

```{r}
#| label: classify-with-ensemble
#| eval: false
```

## Agreement

A code is accepted when at least two of the three models agree, a majority rule chosen for this demonstration (decided by Vagish Hemmige, 27 October 2026); `reviewed_by` records whether the agreement was unanimous or two of three. Codes with no majority are left for the deciders, who fill `final_category` and their initials. Agreement is summarized with Fleiss' kappa.

```{r}
#| label: measure-agreement
#| eval: false
```
